title: Tell no one (Matthew 17:1–13)
hook: a voice that stops mid-song, and three friends face down on a mountain
tomorrow: why would Jesus pay a tax with a coin from a fish's mouth?

segments.voice: Yesterday, Peter said you are the Christ, and heard a promise about the church: the gates shall not prevail. Six days later, three of them climb a mountain.
screen: `THE GATES SHALL NOT PREVAIL.` → `SIX DAYS LATER.`

segments.voice: It happens at recitals, in job interviews, in the middle of a toast: halfway through, the voice just stops, and the room goes very quiet. Three friends on a mountain are in their own version of that moment. Peter, James and John are face down on the ground, too frightened to look up. Minutes ago Jesus' face was shining. Moses and Elias were there, talking with him. Peter, never quiet for long, offered to build something. Then a bright cloud, and a voice out of it. Now nobody is talking. What happens next is very small.
screen: `WHEN THE VOICE JUST STOPS.` → `A BRIGHT CLOUD, A VOICE.` → `FACE DOWN, AFRAID.`

segments.voice: Go back up the mountain a few minutes. Matthew says he was transfigured before them: "his face did shine as the sun, and his raiment was white as the light." Elias is the King James name for Elijah. Peter answers the way people do when something is too big to hold: "Lord, it is good for us to be here," and he offers to put up tabernacles, little shelters, one each. He's still talking when the cloud comes. The voice says, "This is my beloved Son, in whom I am well pleased; hear ye him." Not build for him. Hear him. And they fall on their faces. Here is the answer to the silence. No thunder. "Jesus came and touched them, and said, Arise, and be not afraid." When they look up, the shining is gone, and there's only Jesus, their friend, standing there. The hand comes first; the explanations come later. Then, on the way down, an odd order: "Tell the vision to no man, until the Son of man be risen again from the dead." Keep it quiet, for now. So they carry two things down the mountain: a touch that got them off the ground, and a secret with a date on it.
screen: `HIS FACE DID SHINE AS THE SUN.` · `HEAR YE HIM.` · `HE TOUCHED THEM: ARISE.` · `TELL THE VISION TO NO MAN.` · then, large: `ARISE, BE NOT AFRAID.`

segments.voice: Rest one hand on your own shoulder or forearm, the way you'd steady a friend, and let it stay there, warm and still, while you breathe. If someone you love is near, a hand on their shoulder for a moment, no words, does the same thing. Let the touch come first, before any explaining.
Tell no one. The order on the way down: keep the vision quiet until the Son of man is risen from the dead.
Your line: arise, be not afraid. The hand came before the explanation. See you tomorrow.

screen: `DAY 1457 COUNTS.` → `MATTHEW, READ THROUGH · 31 OF 60.` → `TOMORROW: WHY PAY A TAX WITH A COIN FROM A FISH?`

howItsDone: Some churches keep a feast of the Transfiguration and read this story aloud on it, and some Christians hold on to the words arise, and be not afraid in frightening times.

chat.says: froze mid-solo at rehearsal today. everyone stared. concert's in two weeks. should i just give the solo back?
options: Not yet. On the mountain the first thing was a hand: get up. Sing it once more, scared.
Probably. If you're that afraid, maybe it's a sign the solo isn't meant for you.
Keep it, but tell no one you froze. That's the lesson: keep the hard parts secret.
chat.meaning: Matthew 17:7: Jesus touched them and said, Arise, and be not afraid. The fear was real; the first step was simply getting up.

notes: The word 'Tell no one' is the title's head; the King James wording in 17:9 is 'Tell the vision to no man'. The voice quotes the KJV and uses the title as a summary.
'Six days later' follows Matthew 17:1 ('after six days'). 'There's only Jesus' paraphrases 17:8 ('they saw no man, save Jesus only').
The Elias/John the Baptist exchange (17:10–13) is cited but cut from the voice for length in the story shape.
